taxonomy.name: Pipeline capacity reporting and release
taxonomy.definition: Reporting pipeline deliveries and available capacity to customers and colleagues, and handling capacity release to shippers.

taxonomy.name: Commercial strategy planning
taxonomy.definition: Planning commercial strategy and the yearly plan for a pipeline team, including strategy meetings on projects and customers.

taxonomy.name: Credit report distribution
taxonomy.definition: Preparing and sending the dated credit report on counterparty exposure to the people who rely on it.

taxonomy.name: Price curve and post ID maintenance
taxonomy.definition: Maintaining price curve mappings and the lists of post IDs used to value positions, and circulating updated lists.

taxonomy.name: Customer volume confirmation
taxonomy.definition: Confirming monthly and daily delivered volumes with end-use and utility customers, and agreeing the volumes used for billing.

taxonomy.name: Deal transfer between books
taxonomy.definition: Identifying deals to move, kill or terminate and moving them to another book, such as the bankruptcy books, and reconciling the lists of deals moved.

taxonomy.name: Deal ticket and transport contract set-up
taxonomy.definition: Creating, extending or replacing deal tickets and transport contracts in Sitara so that gas at a meter or on a pipeline has a valid deal for the month.

taxonomy.name: Expense report approval
taxonomy.definition: Submitting and approving employee expense reports and their status changes in the expense system.

taxonomy.name: Gas nomination and nomination changes
taxonomy.definition: Receiving, entering and confirming daily and monthly gas nominations from customers and suppliers, and processing revisions when a party changes its requested volumes.

taxonomy.name: Pipeline imbalance resolution
taxonomy.definition: Reconciling gas imbalances with pipelines and counterparties, exchanging volume statements and agreeing how the imbalance is cleared.

taxonomy.name: Meter flow discrepancy resolution
taxonomy.definition: Investigating gas that flowed at a meter without a matching deal or with unexpected volumes, deciding how the flow is booked, and clearing the unaccounted volume.

taxonomy.name: Month-end close and schedules
taxonomy.definition: Running the accounting month-end close: agreeing the close schedule, releasing and revising closing schedules, and confirming items are complete.

taxonomy.name: Transport contract and OBA negotiation
taxonomy.definition: Negotiating, drafting and approving transportation contracts and operational balancing agreements with shippers and interconnecting pipelines.

taxonomy.name: On-call and holiday coverage
taxonomy.definition: Arranging weekend, holiday and after-hours coverage and handing over on-call notes on what happened during the shift.

taxonomy.name: Performance review
taxonomy.definition: Running staff performance reviews: scheduling PRC meetings and collecting accomplishments and feedback.

taxonomy.name: Pipeline maintenance coordination
taxonomy.definition: Coordinating planned pipeline and meter maintenance, such as pigging, with producers and customers whose meters are affected.

taxonomy.name: P&L and mark-to-market reporting
taxonomy.definition: Producing, reviewing and explaining desk profit and loss and mark-to-market results for traders and management.

taxonomy.name: Real-time power scheduling
taxonomy.definition: Scheduling and correcting real-time power trades, imports and positions with the CAISO and counterparties, and staffing the real-time schedule.

taxonomy.name: Regulatory and market notice review
taxonomy.definition: Reviewing and circulating regulator and ISO notices on market rules, and taking part in the related calls and comment work.

taxonomy.name: Settlement and invoice resolution
taxonomy.definition: Resolving invoices, payments, penalty charges and price disputes with counterparties for gas and power deals.

taxonomy.name: Gas supply cut handling
taxonomy.definition: Responding when a pipeline or supplier cuts scheduled gas: finding the affected deals, rescheduling supply and informing customers.

taxonomy.name: System access requests
taxonomy.definition: Requesting, granting and removing user access and roles in trading and operations systems.

taxonomy.name: System issue resolution
taxonomy.definition: Reporting and fixing errors and changes in operations and trading systems, such as bridge errors, EOL issues and Sitara releases.

taxonomy.name: Time reports and activity surveys
taxonomy.definition: Collecting time reports and hours or activity surveys from staff by their due date.

taxonomy.name: Trading book set-up requests
taxonomy.definition: Requesting, approving and creating new trading books in the risk systems, and confirming the books are ready for deals.

stages.name: score
stages.summary: score: tiers A+B $2,231.13/mo automatable (counted email $526.19 + estimated work $1,704.94), all tiers $2,683.45/mo, observed in 4 mailboxes, 1999-2002; 60 opportunities (13 A, 29 B, 18 C); 2 estimates missing; wrote out/opportunities.json.

rounding: Cents throughout. Whole dollars and hours to one decimal on the page; exact cents one level down.
Each process’s dollars are its counted part’s cents plus its estimated part’s cents, so the rows add up to the total to the cent.

What the page shows adds up, by the largest remainder: each figure gets its whole dollars, and the dollars left over go one each to the figures with the largest cents. The rows in the total share out the headline’s whole dollars this way (the rows below the bar their own total), so the rows add up to the headline and the running total, the sum of the rows above it, ends exactly at it; hours a month are shared out the same way, to one decimal.

Each row’s counted and estimated parts share out that row’s shown dollars, so a row’s parts add up to it; summed down the page, the counted and the estimated columns can differ from the headline’s split by a few dollars.
Where a row’s shown dollars would read as at or over the drafting line while its cents are under it, its status gives the exact cents.
tiers: In the total: seen 10 or more times over 3 or more months by 2 or more staff. 42 processes.
Seen steadily: 40 or more times over 6 or more months by 3 or more staff. 13 processes.
Seen too rarely to count: 18 processes, $452 a month, listed after the total and not in it.
threshold: We draft a working document for every process seen 10 or more times over 3 or more months by 2 or more staff whose automatable work is worth one hour a month ($85) or more.
3 processes clear it with every estimate at its low end, 5 at the middle, 17 at the high end.
The cap of 8 documents and the minimum of 3 are run-time guards; neither bound this run.
estimates: One estimate per process: hands-on minutes a round (low, middle, high) and the share of that work that could be automated.
Proposed once by the synthesizer agent (model opus, effort medium, set in its agent definition) from 3 to 12 cited quotes from 2 or more senders, for a process seen 3 or more times.
Checked by code: no more than 480 minutes a round or 80% automatable, every citation real, never one sender alone. Cached, and overridable from a file without a model call.
58 estimates accepted, 0 set by the project team, 2 missing.
identity: One person’s several addresses fold into one by a published rule, each fold only onto a unique candidate: 57 folds, each listed by rule.
Left apart: 30 m..last addresses with several candidates, 25 with one candidate but no middle initial to confirm it, 1 refused because the two share a message, 36 with no candidate.
26 distribution lists and 9 system senders are never staff.
A round tagged with two processes is shared between them.
A contradiction in the run’s summaries is dropped when every owner claim it cites names one and the same person: 0 contradictions dropped on this run; the rest are shown beside the claims they cite.
